**Lagoa da Conceição** – the heart of the island. It’s a short walk to the beach, has the 300‑500 Mbps fiber network that runs R$100‑150/month in most neighborhoods [1], and is considered one of the safer, most walkable districts.  

**Campeche** – another beachfront enclave with easy pedestrian access to the shore. It shares the same high‑speed internet infrastructure as Lagoa and is frequently cited as a safe, family‑friendly spot [1][5].  

**Residencial Lídia Milani** (near Ingleses) – the apartment listings in this area sit just 0.25 km from the beach and are part of a residential block that offers free Wi‑Fi and reliable fiber, with a typical speed of 300‑500 Mbps [3].  

**Ingleses Beach** – the flat on this block is a short walk from Ingleses Beach and only 5.3 km from the waterpark, making it convenient for beach days while staying close to fast internet [3].  

The main central neighborhoods—**Centro, Lagoa, Campeche, and Jurerê**—all have the fiber optic coverage mentioned above and are generally regarded as safe and walkable, though exact crime rates vary by block [5].

answer_raw:
For a six‑month stay, the most reliable options are **Lagoa da Conceição**, **Campeche**, and the **Residencial Lídia Milani** area near Ingleses Beach.

- **Lagoa da Conceição** – a safe, walkable district, just **0.25 km** to the beach, with fiber speeds of **300–500 Mbps** and a monthly cost of **R$100–150**. [1][3]
- **Campeche** – beachfront, family‑friendly, same fiber speeds, and considered safe. [1][5]
- **Residencial Lídia Milani (Ingleses)** – a **0.25 km** walk from the beach; the listed flat offers **free Wi-Fi**, **free parking**, a **full kitchen**, and a **flat-screen TV** [3]. Fast fiber internet (**300–500 Mbps**) runs **R$100–150/month** [1]. The airport is **19–38 km** away [3]. [3][1]

Safety and walkability: precise crime statistics aren’t provided; check local police reports or community forums. Public transit works well only near the six integration terminals; away from these, life without a car is more time-consuming. [1][5]

Jurerê is mentioned in the guide, but fiber coverage and safety details are not confirmed; verify these before deciding. [5]
